sources.title: Robert C. Senior: Indo-Scythian Dynasty, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Specialist article directly read. Uses broad migrations, multiple rulers and mixed coin imagery only; its disputed detailed chronologies for Maues, Azes and Nahapana are not adopted. Northwestern succession distinguished from continuing Western Kshatrapas.

sources.title: British Museum: Red sandstone pillar capital, Google Arts and Culture collection entry
sources.note: Museum-authored collection entry directly indexed/read: queen of Rajula donates stupa with Buddha relics; satrap genealogy. Personal name omitted because modern scholarship disputes its reading. Neelis consulted but not used for public copy because existing Vakataka card already substantially draws on the same work.

sources.title: British Museum: Pandit Bhagvanlal Indraji
sources.note: Museum biography directly indexed/read: nineteenth-century scholar, capital discovery, Gujarati scholarship, numismatic studies and bequest. No exact discovery year or controlled excavation claim.

sources.title: CSMVS: King Nahapana, silver coin, object 22.459
sources.note: Museum object directly read: 18 mm, 1.92 g, portrait, three scripts, arrow/pellet/thunderbolt. Catalogue dating not used because Nahapana chronology is disputed; do not mistake Greek lettering for fluent Greek language.

sources.title: e-PG Pathshala: Western Kshatrapa Coinage, An Introduction
sources.note: University teaching module directly read: PDF pp.4-6, Nahapana overstrikes, Kardamaka line, dated coin genealogies and Gupta replacement. Contested early absolute chronology and claim of unique dating are omitted.

sources.title: e-PG Pathshala: Junagadh Inscription of Rudradaman
sources.note: Direct PDF read, sections 3, 5 and 5.1-5.5. Royal eulogy distinguished from independent proof of benevolence. Conflicting breach dimensions in module not repeated; no first Sanskrit inscription claim.

sources.title: Andrew Ollett: Language of the Snakes (2017)
sources.note: Publisher open-access monograph directly read, printed pp.39-42 and table1. Ushavadata donation, water/rest houses, field, Sanskrit versus Middle Indic. No contested precise Nahapana dates adopted.

sources.title: John Steven Stavrellis: Sectarianism and Heresy in Early Puranic Descriptions of the Kali Yuga (2023)
sources.note: Bonn dissertation directly read, PDF page84 and notes35-37: 3000 karshapanas split between two weavers guilds; interest for robes and daily needs; permanent endowment. No universal first banking claim and no assertion the loan was gold.

sources.title: Federico De Romanis: Notes on Barygaza’s Trade (2025)
sources.note: Author university repository full chapter directly read, printed pp.121 and127-129. Periplus commodity lists interpreted as port trade, not household menu or universal consumption. Slavery is explicitly identified in the primary merchant account.

sources.title: Steven E. Sidebotham and colleagues: Indians in Roman Berenike (2025)
sources.note: Original DAI article exact indexed PDF text read, printed p.274, paragraph101 and note191. Direct whole PDF exceeds tool extraction limit. Reproducible query: site.publications.dainst.org "rājño rudradāmasa" "Andhau". Quotes and translates Andhau Prakrit dating formula, following Mirashi1981 no.46 p.118. Berenike itself is not treated as a Saka colony.

proposedOverrides.name: Saka kingdoms in India
proposedOverrides.summary: Regional Saka rulers and Western Kshatrapas connected Indian cities, religious patrons and long-distance trade.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Exact indexed record only. No alias absorption. Separate saces is a Central Asian polygon and remains independent; steppe scythians is also distinct.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Four identical HB polygons, world-bc1, world-100, world-200, world-300; bbox66.43326433264335,18.21632352593194,79.63819638196384,33.655800818654086. Broad outline spans northwest and western India; not a verified single state at every date.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Early Indo-Scythian rulers predate imported start. Distinct northwestern/Mathura and Western Kshatrapa phases are explained publicly. Nahapana chronology is disputed; no exact reign dates used. Andhau writing130/131CE and Junagadh circa150CE securely contextualized. Early fifth-century Gupta replacement may postdate atlas endpoint.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: No generic steppe nomadic household practices projected into India. Sources support travel water, monastic provision, crafts and food trade; no household toilet or medical regimen asserted. Royal tax relief and accomplishments attributed to eulogy. No uncontrolled reconstruction of original Brahmi glyphs.
